Kenapa gunung api bisa meledak?Kenapa ada gunung api yang meledak, kayak Merapi, sementara yang lain lavanya cuma mengalir?

PromiseGunung api meledak karena gas: di kedalaman, gas larut di magma karena tekanan tinggi; waktu magma naik dan tekanannya turun, gas lepas jadi gelembung yang membesar, dan di magma yang kental seperti Merapi gelembung itu terjebak sampai tekanannya cukup untuk meledak dan menghancurkan magma jadi abu.
AudiencePelajar SMA di Indonesia dan orang dewasa yang penasaran. Mereka tinggal di negeri gunung api, tahu Merapi dan kata 'magma', dan banyak yang mengira gunung meledak karena panas atau api di dalamnya, bukan karena gas.
Length57.5 s · 18 shots · 48 drawn frames · 1920×1080 · 60 fps · id · captions only
LookLow Poly template (Faceted 3D) · #ff9f1c
The Low Poly template, line by line: a faceted 3D world (hills, sky, objects built from flat triangles) under a soft gradient sky; one directional sun, so every facet has its own flat shade, and soft fog toward the horizon; one harmonious palette per scene (dawn for Merapi: orange #ff9f1c, sand #ffbf69, sky #cbf3f0, teal #2ec4b6, dark #293241; midday teal for Hawaii; a warm-dark ember palette inside the magma); flat-shaded facets with no textures, water, glass and the soda bottle slightly transparent; Merapi and Kīlauea built from their real terrain profiles at true scale with a few hundred triangles each, a cross-section as a sliced faceted model; Nunito with a slight drop shadow; captions two or three words at a time on a soft translucent panel at the bottom centre, the key word in the accent; floating tags with lines to the object; numbers at their real values; charts as faceted bars; slow drone-like orbits, fly-throughs and push-ins with gentle easing; objects assemble facet by facet and the world reshapes smoothly; cuts by flying through a cloud or over a hill; soft fog, a very light bloom on the sun, no grain; never smooth high-poly models, photo textures or cluttered scenes. Everything that must be read sits above y 850 and inside 80 px side margins; the caption panel sits at y 862 to 950.
The storyboard passes the standard: 18 shots, 48 drawn frames, 12 facts, 6 acts.

Fact sheet

IdClaimSource
f1Magma is molten rock below the surface (lava once it erupts); besides a little crystal and rock it contains dissolved gases. It collects in a reservoir below the volcano and reaches the surface through a conduit (the central vent). On screen: 'magma: batu cair', 'saluran magma', 'kawah'.USGS, Robert I. Tilling, 'Volcanoes' (General Interest Publication, pubs.usgs.gov/gip/volc/): 'Molten rock below the surface of the Earth that rises in volcanic vents is known as magma, but after it erupts from a volcano it is called lava ... the ascending magma commonly contains some crystals, fragments of surrounding (unmelted) rocks, and dissolved gases'; 'The essential feature of a composite volcano is a conduit system through which magma from a reservoir deep in the Earth's crust rises to the surface'.
f2Magma rises because it is lighter than the solid rock around it. On screen: 'lebih ringan, jadi naik'.USGS, Tilling, 'Volcanoes': 'Driven by buoyancy and gas pressure the molten rock, which is lighter than the surrounding solid rock forces its way upward'.
f3The gas in magma is mostly water vapour, followed by carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide (with smaller amounts of others). At Merapi's summit fumarole in 2010 the gas was 87-92% water vapour, 5.6-10% CO₂ and 0.8-1.0% SO₂ (mol %). On screen: tags 'uap air (H₂O)', 'CO₂', 'SO₂'; most molecules drawn are water.USGS Open-File Report 95-85, McGee & Gerlach, 'Volcanic gas': 'Water vapor is typically the most abundant volcanic gas, followed by carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide' (also OFR 97-262, McGee et al.); Surono et al. 2012, J. Volcanol. Geotherm. Res. 241-242, Table 1 (Woro fumarole analyses, May and September 2010).
f4All magmas contain dissolved gases; as magma rises the confining pressure falls and the gases come out of solution, like the gas in a closed bottle of a fizzy drink that forms bubbles when the pressure is released. On screen: the soda bottle, 'Kayak soda dalam botol tertutup', 'tutup rapat: tekanan tinggi', 'tekanan tinggi menahan gasnya tetap larut', 'begitu magma naik, tekanannya turun', 'gasnya lepas jadi gelembung'. Simplification: 'tekanan' on the gauge is shown without numbers; the weight of the rock above is what sets it.USGS, Tilling, 'Volcanoes': 'All magmas contain dissolved gases, and as they rise to the surface to erupt, the confining pressures are reduced and the dissolved gases are liberated either quietly or explosively' and 'Gases in lava may be compared with the gas in a bottle of a carbonated soft drink'; British Geological Survey, 'Eruption styles' (bgs.ac.uk): 'It's a bit like a bottle of fizzy pop'.
f5The bubbles expand as the pressure keeps falling, and their sudden expansion is what drives explosions. On screen: 'Makin ke atas, makin besar' (the bubble chart is marked 'ilustrasi' and has no numbers), 'tekanannya numpuk terus'.USGS, Tilling, 'Volcanoes': 'Their sudden expansion causes the terrible explosions that throw out great masses of solid rock as well as lava, dust, and ashes'; 'Explosive eruptions caused by gas rapidly expanding and escaping from molten lava'.
f6Whether the gas escapes quietly or explosively depends on the magma: in thin, runny magma the gas escapes easily and the lava flows out; in thick, sticky magma it cannot move freely, pressure builds and it escapes with explosive violence. On screen: 'Kalau encer, gasnya lolos', 'gas lolos', 'Kalau kental, gasnya terjebak', 'mengalir', 'meledak'.USGS, Tilling, 'Volcanoes': 'If the lava is a thin fluid (not viscous), the gases may escape easily. But if the lava is thick and pasty (highly viscous), the gases will not move freely but will build up tremendous pressure, and ultimately escape with explosive violence'; British Geological Survey, 'Eruption styles': 'If a magma has low viscosity (it is runny), gas can escape easily, so when the magma erupts at the surface it forms lava flows'.
f7In an explosive eruption the gas-filled froth of magma is shattered into small fragments: volcanic ash. On screen: '...sampai meledak. Magmanya hancur jadi abu.', 'magma hancur jadi abu'.USGS, Tilling, 'Volcanoes': 'The violent separation of gas from lava may produce rock froth called pumice ... In many eruptions, the froth is shattered explosively into small fragments that are hurled high into the air in the form of volcanic cinders, volcanic ash, and volcanic dust'.
f8Kīlauea is a shield volcano built of fluid basalt lava flows; the Hawaiian shields are generally non-explosive, so its lava usually flows out. On screen: 'Tapi di Hawaii, lavanya mengalir', 'Kīlauea, Hawaii', 'mengalir'. Simplification: the source says 'generally' non-explosive; the film shows the usual behaviour and does not claim Kīlauea never explodes.USGS, Tilling, 'Volcanoes': shield volcanoes 'are built almost entirely of fluid lava flows ... the Hawaiian Islands are composed of linear chains of these volcanoes including Kilauea and Mauna Loa', and 'the generally non-explosive Hawaiian shield volcanoes'. Profile: AWS Terrain Tiles (reference/profil-merapi-kilauea.png).
f9Merapi is a stratovolcano about 2,910 m high on the border of Central Java and Yogyakarta, 25-30 km north of Yogyakarta. Its magma is basaltic andesite (55.8% SiO₂ in 2010), and it typically builds viscous lava domes that plug the top of the conduit. On screen: 'Merapi', 'Magma Merapi itu yang kental', 'magma kental: andesit basaltik', 'kubah lava menyumbat', '2,9 km'.Kementerian ESDM (Badan Geologi, PVMBG/BPPTKG), 'Mengenal Merapi Lebih Dekat: Merapi Dulu dan Kini' (esdm.go.id): Merapi 2,910 m, a stratovolcano (height quoted from the search summary of the same page); Surono et al. 2012: 'Merapi stratovolcano is located 25-30 km north of ... Yogyakarta ... composed mainly of basaltic-andesite', 'produced viscous lava domes', 'lava domes have typically plugged the uppermost part of the conduit', Table 1 SiO₂ 55.8 wt% (2010).
f10Merapi's 2010 eruption was its largest since 1872 (VEI about 4); the climactic explosion on 4 November 2010 sent an ash column to 17 km altitude. Mount Everest is 8,848.86 m, so the column rose 17 ÷ 8.85 ≈ 1.9 times as high: 'hampir 2× Everest'. On screen: 'Merapi, 2010', 'Tahun 2010, abunya sampai 17 km', '17 km', '8,8 km', 'hampir 2× Everest'.Surono et al. 2012, 'The 2010 explosive eruption of Java's Merapi volcano, a 100-year event', J. Volcanol. Geotherm. Res. 241-242: 121-135 (read in full: 'a VEI and Me of about 4'; 'produced an ash column that ascended to 17 km altitude'; the 1872 eruption named as the previous large explosive one); 'largest in more than a century': the USGS publication summary of the same paper (via search); Everest: Nepal and China's joint announcement of 8 December 2020 (The Kathmandu Post, 'It's official: Mount Everest is 8,848.86 metres tall'; NPR, same day).
f11Merapi's silhouette is its real profile: the west-east terrain profile through the summit sampled every 0.5 km (summit 2,915 m in the data; 1,441 m 3 km west; 1,455 m 3 km east; a shoulder of 2,481-2,417 m 1-1.5 km east), drawn at true scale (230 px per km both ways in s01, cropped to the part above 1,000 m). Since 2010 the summit crater opens to the south-east.AWS Terrain Tiles (Mapzen terrarium, SRTM-derived), zoom 12, sampled for this film (reference/profil-merapi-kilauea.png); crater opening: Kementerian ESDM, 'Mengenal Merapi Lebih Dekat' ('terbentuk kawah yang membuka ke arah tenggara/selatan').
f12The cut-away drawings (s04, s07, s08, s13, s14) are schematic: the reservoir, conduit and dome are drawn to show where things are, not their real sizes or depths, and the screen says 'skema · tidak sesuai skala'. Their layout follows the USGS drawings of a composite volcano and a lava dome.USGS, Tilling, 'Volcanoes', figures 'Schematic representation of the internal structure of a typical composite volcano' and '... of a typical volcanic dome' (pubs.usgs.gov/gip/volc/types.html; copies in reference/).

Music

Composed for this film (to be made with kit/audio/music.mjs after the board is approved; not generated yet) · 72 BPM · An ambient bed composed for the film, as the template's Sound line asks: a warm pad, soft wind, gentle chimes (kalimba and small bells) on the tags and cards, a slow pulse at 72 BPM, 57.5 s plus a tail that the mix lays over frame 0 so the loop is seamless. It sinks into a low warm drone inside the magma (s05 to s10), tightens with a slow rising tone under the pressure (s12 to s14), and swells after one deep, soft boom on the eruption (s15); it resolves on the recap. Every shot starts on a beat. Effects per shot are in each shot's 'sound': a muffled rumble under the opening column, surf and a lava gurgle for Kīlauea, a glassy clink for the bottle, soft presses and gauge ticks for pressure, sparse bubbling, light pops for the runny column, a thick creak for the trapped one, stony clicks and cracks for the dome. Nothing loud or harsh: a calm explainer, not a disaster film.

Teaches
The explosion: the gas bursts out and tears the frothy magma into ash.
On screen
The dome blows apart into faceted blocks; the frothy magma under it shatters into tiny dark triangular fragments (ash) carried up by the gas; the camera pulls back through the cut-away to the whole of Merapi in its dawn world, the faceted ash column rising from the summit as in s01. Tag 'magma hancur jadi abu' on the fragments.
Camera
A fast-then-easing pull back: from the dome at 85 mm to the s01 framing (the whole mountain, 35 mm), the cut-away closing up as it goes so the mountain is whole again; the column in focus.
Motion
Main move: the burst (blocks fly out on curves, fragments stream up) and the pull back. Supporting: the column assembles puff by puff. Detail: a shock ring of facets in the sky.
Carries on
The rising ash column over Merapi.
Transition
Cut to the chart: the column becomes the tallest bar.
Sound
One deep, soft boom (felt more than heard), then a long rushing rumble; the bed swells.
Check
The fragments come from the magma (they are dark and angular), not from the sky; the mountain is whole again by the end.

Teaches
How big that was: Merapi's 2010 ash column reached 17 km, almost twice the height of Everest.
On screen
A faceted bar chart standing on the plain (the template's 'charts as faceted bars'), heights at their real values on one scale (40 px per km above sea level): Merapi itself 2.9 km, Everest 8.8 km, and Merapi's ash column of 4 November 2010, 17 km, in the accent. Values written on top of each bar; a tag 'hampir 2× Everest'.
Camera
A low, slow dolly along the bars from left to right, 35 mm, ending square to the tallest; the 17 km bar in focus.
Motion
The bars rise one by one, facet layers stacking, each stopping at its value (no counting through false values: the number appears when the bar is complete). The tallest rises last, on the beat.
Carries on
The 17 km bar.
Transition
The bars fold down into three small cards for the recap.
Sound
A soft rising chime per bar, the third one fuller.
Check
Bars at 116, 354 and 680 px: 2.9 : 8.8 : 17 km.

Teaches
The whole chain in one frame: dissolved gas, rising magma and bubbles, trapped in thick magma, explosion.
On screen
Three soft translucent cards across the frame over a blurred dawn world, each with a tiny faceted scene and two or three words: (1) the reservoir with dissolved molecules and a pressing arrow, 'gas larut'; (2) the conduit with bubbles growing upward, 'magma naik, gelembung'; (3) Merapi with its dome bursting into a column, 'kental: terjebak, meledak' with 'meledak' in the accent.
Motion
The cards fly in one per beat on gentle curves and settle; each little scene plays its one move once (molecules drift, bubbles rise and grow, the dome bursts).
Carries on
The third card's little Merapi.
Transition
The third card grows to fill the frame and the camera flies over a faceted hill into the opening picture.
Sound
Three gentle chimes rising; the bed resolves.
Check
Readable with the sound off; the three words carry the chain in order.
